hints: Focus on counting atoms carefully from the skeletal ring, remembering each corner is a carbon with enough hydrogens to make four bonds.
Count the carbons, bromines and hydrogens to get the molecular formula, then simplify it to the lowest ratio for statement 1.
Think about the shape of large saturated rings with tetrahedral carbons, and check what makes a carbon chiral to judge statements 2 and 3.
walkthrough:
**Find the molecular formula**

Look at the skeleton. It is a 12-membered ring, so there are 12 carbons.

There are 6 $\text{Br}$ atoms shown. Each $\text{C-Br}$ carbon has 1 H, each $\text{CH}_2$ carbon has 2 H. That gives $6 \times 1 + 6 \times 2 = 18$ H.

**Check statement 1, empirical formula**

Molecular formula is $\text{C}_{12}\text{H}_{18}\text{Br}_6$.

$$\text{C}_{12}\text{H}_{18}\text{Br}_6 \div 6 = \text{C}_2\text{H}_3\text{Br}$$
So statement 1 is correct.

**Check statement 2, shape of the ring**

All ring carbons are $sp^3$ with tetrahedral bond angles of about $109.5^{\circ}$.

A flat 12-membered ring would have huge angle strain and clashing atoms, so it puckers into a non-planar conformation. So statement 2 is correct.

**Check statement 3, chiral carbons**

A chiral carbon has four different groups: here $\text{Br}$, $\text{H}$, and two different ring segments going clockwise and anticlockwise.

Each of the six $\text{C-Br}$ carbons meets this test, so there are six chiral centres. So statement 3 is correct.

**Combine the conclusions**

Statements 1, 2 and 3 are all correct.

That matches the combination for 1, 2 and 3 correct.

options.A: Correct because all three statements are true. Molecular formula $\text{C}_{12}\text{H}_{18}\text{Br}_6$ simplifies to $\text{C}_2\text{H}_3\text{Br}$, the large $sp^3$ ring must be puckered and non-planar, and all six $\text{C-Br}$ carbons are chiral.
options.B: Wrong because it includes only 1 and 2. Statement 3 is also true, each brominated carbon is bonded to Br, H and two non-identical paths around the ring, so it is chiral.
options.C: Wrong because it includes only 2 and 3. Statement 1 is also true, the 12:18:6 ratio simplifies exactly to $\text{C}_2\text{H}_3\text{Br}$.
options.D: Wrong because it includes only 1. Statements 2 and 3 are also true. Students choosing this often doubt the non-planar shape or miss the chirality of the $\text{C-Br}$ carbons.
